con-vexo , āvi, ātum, 1,
I.v. a., to press or squeeze together (post-class., and perh. only in the foll. exs.): (multitudo) me male
miseram convexavit, Soror Appii Caeci in Gell. 10, 6, 2: “animal,” Veg. Art. Vet. 3, 18, 6 : “membra,” id. ib. 4, 25, 1 : “ilia cursu nimio,” id. ib. 3, 65, 3 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
